title: A Person I Admire
description: Practise the present perfect and relative clauses, then write an article about someone who inspires you.
instructions: Do the exercises in Part 1. Then write your text in Part 2.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: My aunt is a doctor ___ work takes her all over the world.
exercises.explanation: Use "whose" to show possession: a doctor whose work = a doctor + her work.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: She ___ (help) hundreds of people in her career.
answers: has helped
's helped
exercises.explanation: Use the present perfect for experiences and achievements when we do not say exactly when: she has helped.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: The person who I most admire is my grandmother.
My grandmother is the person who I most admire.
exercises.explanation: The relative clause "who I most admire" comes straight after "the person".

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: She has started her own company in 2015.
answers: She started her own company in 2015.
exercises.explanation: With a past date like "in 2015", use the past simple: she started.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: She had very little money. ___, she never gave up.
exercises.explanation: "However" introduces something surprising or contrasting after the previous sentence.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: If I ___ (be) as brave as her, I would travel the world.
answers: were
was
exercises.explanation: In the second conditional, use the past simple after "if". "Were" is used with all persons, especially in writing: If I were.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: I have known her since five years.
answers: I have known her for five years.
I've known her for five years.
exercises.explanation: Use "for" with a period of time (five years) and "since" with a starting point (since 2020).

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word WHO. Begin: "I admire my uncle ..."
exercises.text: I admire my uncle. He climbed Mount Everest.
answers: I admire my uncle, who climbed Mount Everest.
I admire my uncle, who has climbed Mount Everest.
exercises.explanation: Use "who" to join two sentences about the same person. "Who" replaces "he".

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: When she was younger, my aunt ___ work in a hospital in Kenya.
exercises.explanation: Use "used to + infinitive" for past habits and situations that are not true now.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the word in brackets.
exercises.text: She is one of the most ___ (create) people I know.
answers: creative
exercises.explanation: We need an adjective after "the most". The adjective from "create" is "creative".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: She enjoys learning new languages.
exercises.explanation: Some verbs, such as enjoy, finish and mind, are followed by the -ing form: enjoys learning.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: She works more hard than anyone else in our family.
answers: She works harder than anyone else in our family.
exercises.explanation: "Hard" is a short word, so the comparative is "harder", not "more hard".

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: As a nurse, she ___ work at night twice a week.
exercises.explanation: Use "have to / has to" + infinitive for obligations, especially rules of a job. With "she" use "has to".

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word UP. Begin: "She never ..."
exercises.text: She never stopped trying, even when things were hard.
answers: She never gave up, even when things were hard.
She never gave up trying, even when things were hard.
exercises.explanation: "Give up" means to stop trying. The past simple is "gave up".

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with one word.
exercises.text: She trained every day. As a ___, she won a gold medal.
answers: result
exercises.explanation: "As a result" introduces the consequence of what happened before.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: She has ___ written her third book, and it comes out next month.
exercises.explanation: Use "just" between "has/have" and the past participle for something that happened a very short time ago.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: She is the most generous person I know.
exercises.explanation: Long adjectives form the superlative with "the most": the most generous person.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: She has always wanted helping people in need.
answers: She has always wanted to help people in need.
exercises.explanation: "Want" is followed by the to-infinitive, not the -ing form: wanted to help.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word USED. Begin: "My grandfather ..."
exercises.text: My grandfather was a fisherman, but he isn't now.
answers: My grandfather used to be a fisherman.
exercises.explanation: Use "used to + infinitive" for a past situation that is no longer true.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word THAN. Begin: "My mother ..."
exercises.text: Nobody in my family is as patient as my mother.
answers: My mother is more patient than anyone else in my family.
My mother is more patient than anyone in my family.
My mother is more patient than anybody else in my family.
My mother is more patient than anybody in my family.
My mother is more patient than everyone else in my family.
My mother is more patient than everybody else in my family.
exercises.explanation: Long adjectives form the comparative with "more ... than": more patient than anyone else.

task.prompt: An international students' magazine is running a series called "People who inspire us". Write an article about a person you admire.
contentPoints: Say who the person is and how you know them.
Describe what they have done or achieved.
Explain the qualities you admire in them.
Say what you have learned from them.
usefulLanguage: The person I admire most is ...
task.modelAnswer:
My Grandmother, My Hero

The person I admire most is my grandmother, Rosa. She is seventy-five, but she is more active than most people I know.

When she was young, her family was very poor, and she had to leave school at fourteen. However, she never gave up. She worked in a factory during the day and studied at night. At the age of thirty, she opened a small bakery, which is still the most popular one in our village.

What I admire most is her energy and her kindness. Although she works hard, she always has time for other people. She has helped many young people who needed a job.

She has taught me that it is never too late to follow your dreams. I hope I will be as brave as her one day.
